# Demo dataset — `server_metrics`

**Generated by:** `python -m demos.datasets.server_metrics.generate`
**Output:** `server_metrics.csv`

**Shape:** 1440 rows × 5 columns (one full day at 1-minute resolution).

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `minute` | Minute of day (0–1439). |
| `cpu` | Fraction of CPU used (0.0–1.0). |
| `mem_gb` | Resident memory (GB). |
| `p99_ms` | p99 request latency (ms). |
| `req_s` | Requests per second. |

## Known finding (the "2 a.m. save")

- **Baseline** (~96% of the timeline): mild diurnal sinusoid. p99
  hovers around 38 ms, memory ~12 GB, CPU 34% mean.
- **Drift starts at minute 1382** (~96% in): memory creeps up, CPU
  follows, p99 latency explodes, throughput drops. Classic
  "memory leak / hot-loop" regime shift.
- **End state at minute 1439:** mem ~16 GB (+30%), p99 ~116 ms
  (3× baseline), CPU ~50%, req/s down ~27%.

## Expected Aurora findings

- **HMM / Regimes:** two latent states; the transition lands ~1380.
- **Hampel z-score:** at least 3 CRITICAL anomalies on `p99_ms` in
  the last ~30 minutes.
- **Granger:** `mem_gb → p99_ms` and `cpu → p99_ms` directional.
- **Forecast:** p99 trajectory continues to climb.

## Use in demos

- **Demo 3 — The Save:** stream this dataset at 60× speed so the
  full day plays in ~24 seconds. The contract trips on
  `findings.crit_count >= 3` at the regime shift; Slack ping is
  the climax.

## Replay command

```powershell
python -m demos.replay demos\datasets\server_metrics\server_metrics.csv `
  --to demos\_live\server.csv `
  --speed 60 `
  --start-rows 200
```
